## Prep

### Purpose of the piece

- **Who it is for:** procurement leads and the executives who sign off AI purchases in Australian agencies.
- **What they should do afterwards:** add three questions to every AI tender.

### Key points to argue

1. **Procurement shapes AI use more than policy does.** The contract sets the terms.

<!-- body -->
## Why procurement matters

Most Australian agencies now buy AI rather than build it. The contract is therefore where obligations are set, and it is often the only document a vendor reads closely.

Voluntary guidance has changed board behaviour across the ASX 200. In an era of rapid technological change, organisations face new questions about who is accountable when a model fails, and many of those questions are never written down anywhere that a vendor would see them before signing.

## Three questions for every tender

First, who owns the model's outputs once it is deployed?[^1] Second, what monitoring does the vendor commit to? Third, how is the contract ended if the model degrades?

| Question | Who answers | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ownership | Legal | Before award |
| Monitoring | Vendor | Quarterly |

⟦SPECIFIC NEEDED: a named agency example⟧

[^1]: Department of Finance, *Policy for the responsible use of AI in government*, 2024.
